Standard robot-cell handshake register map: R[41]=override/EDA, DO[8]=station handshake pulse, DI[40]=cycle stop, DI[39]=station fault (into R[1]), RO[1]/RO[2] triggered via CALL GRIP/UNGRIP subs rather than direct output writes.

name: picktool  quick setup guide.pdf
location: \\…\Electrical Dept\Standards - Software\Fanuc Robot\Claude Fanuc Assets\Prompting & Instructions\picktool  quick setup guide.pdf
takeaways: Line tracking requires a physical Pulsecoder (conveyor encoder) wired to the robot controller and configured with an encoder number + moving-average smoothing (typically 10 updates) so the robot stops smoothly if the conveyor stops suddenly.

The tracking frame is defined by measuring two points on the conveyor (upstream/downstream boundaries) with a calibration grid plus a recorded Z height — this defines the window within which the robot can pick moving parts.

Robot programs must set 'Continue track at prog end' = TRUE, or tracking motion stops jerkily between program calls — this is the standard setting for continuous smooth operation, not a one-off tuning choice.

Vision-guided pick positions are computed as a nominal taught position offset by a vision-found VOFFSET register (VR) — the vision system doesn't reteach positions, it offsets a fixed one per detected part.

Payload is switched at runtime between two profiles (hand-only vs hand+workpiece) right after grip/release — same idea as an SDC gripper's mass compensation, but done via FANUC's PAYLOAD[n] register swap.

Conveyor/fixed-station handoff uses a queue abstraction (station ID + GETQUE/ACKQUE calls) rather than direct position polling — this is FANUC's built-in equivalent of a station-to-station part handoff.

Auto visual track frame setup is restricted to 4-axis robots, line conveyors only (not circular/servo), one robot group, up to 8 conveyors per system — hard vendor limitations, not configuration choices.

name: EtherNetIPSampleProgramGuide(CompactLogix).pdf
takeaways: On read failure the result-data tag is updated with literal "ERROR" rather than leaving stale data.

Handshake-enabled result retrieval uses a strobe/latch pattern: PLC sets ResultDataLatch true to request data, reader responds with ResultDataStrobe true when data is updated, PLC then drops the latch bit — this is a generic explicit-request/strobe pattern, not unique to vision cameras.
This reader's protocol is structurally the same trigger→busy-wait→complete→clear pattern SDC already uses for vision-system integrations — it's a barcode-reader instance of that same device class.

SR-Reader is a barcode/2D code reader talking EtherNet/IP, controlled by a fixed 4-step PLC sequence: check ready (Busy/Error) → set Trigger true to start read → detect Read Complete → access Result Data.

Two handshake modes: Data Handshake Disable = reader auto-pushes Result Data the instant read completes, no retrieve step; Data Handshake Enable = reader queues results internally and PLC must pulse a Retrieve/Latch request to pull each queued result, with an update/ready count exposing backlog.

Read Complete has its own acknowledge cycle — PLC sets Read Complete Clear true once Read Complete is seen true, then false once Read Complete drops false — this arms the reader for the next trigger; skipping the clear pulse stalls the next read.

Read Failure is a separate bit from Read Complete — Result Data still updates on failure, just populated with an ERROR value, so the read-success/read-failure branches both land on 'complete', they just check the failure bit before trusting the payload.

Reading Mode Single + Timing Mode Level Trigger means the trigger input must stay high to sustain the read attempt and going low cancels the in-progress read — this is a level trigger, not a one-shot pulse.

name: Fanuc_Dual_Arm_VIS_Calibration_Guide.docx
takeaways: SDC standard reverses common Fanuc training convention: camera mounts on the FOLLOWER (Group 2), calibration target mounts on the LEADER (Group 1) — gives the follower freedom to sweep poses while the leader holds the target still.
UT9 is reserved cell-wide on all SDC dual-arm cells for calibration tools only (camera UTOOL and target UTOOL) — production tools live in UT1–UT8 and must never be overwritten by calibration data.

MultiCal (Fanuc's automated calibration program) is the SDC-preferred execution path over manual pose-by-pose capture; run at 25-50% override, T1 mandatory on first attempt of any new cell, one parameter change at a time on failure.
Results are NOT saved until manually accepted from MultiCal's bottom page — a completed run that isn't accepted silently discards the calibration and leaves the Coord Motion page stale.
Residual error acceptance bands: <0.5mm excellent (precision welding/dispensing), 0.5-1.0mm acceptable for handling/assembly, 1.0-2.0mm marginal (investigate), >2.0mm reject and recalibrate.
Inside a COORD block, follower motion lines are interpreted in the leader's UFRAME, not the follower's own $WORLD — a common source of programmer confusion when teaching points.

Re-calibration triggers: any collision, re-mastering or motor/encoder replacement on either arm, lens/focus/aperture adjustment, or loosening of camera/grid mounting hardware; scheduled every 6mo (production) / quarterly (high-precision).

takeaways: Valve spool configuration is chosen by axis motion type: horizontal PNP axes/grippers use 2-position double-solenoid (SY3200); vertical PNP axes use 3-position CENTER-BLOCKED (SY3300) so the axis holds position rather than falling on air/power loss.
3-position center-EXHAUST valves (SY3400) are reserved for advanced safety applications that must actively depressurize an actuator, not general motion.

Standalone (non-valve-bank) valves are required when a robot gripper has no internal solenoid (Epson robots never have this option; Fanuc can) or when an actuator needs high-speed direct-PLC-output control bypassing the valve bank.
Air prep unit sizing = total machine air consumption + 20% safety factor; number of air prep units/valve banks scales with number of machine safety zones.
Vacuum generation is a deliberate engineer's choice between two SMC families: ZK2 electronic generator (integrated pressure switch) vs ZH venturi (standalone Coval switch) — sized per application.
EX600 (EtherNet/IP, up to 9 IO modules/16 valves) is the primary valve-bank platform; EX260 (IO-Link) is used when the machine's I/O architecture is IO-Link and has no expansion IO capability.

name: SDC_Motors_Cables_Drives_Guildelines_Rev 2.docx
takeaways: TLP motors (Kinetix 5300) are SDC's default for simple point-to-point axes — standard PNP, ball screw/belt, simple rotary, indexing ring shot-pin.
VPL motors (Kinetix 5500) are for complex/coordinated motion — dial/CAM axes, indexing ring main drive, servo press, high-speed coordinated motion.
SDC standard encoder is multiturn absolute (not incremental) — position is retained through power cycles, which is why homing-move logic can be minimal.
Holding brakes are required for vertical loads EXCEPT the SDC standard PNP vertical axis, which does not need one for standard payloads (heavy payloads need a calc).
TLP requires separate power+feedback cables; VPL uses a single hybrid cable (Lutze preferred); motion axes need high-flex cable.
CIP Motion-enabled PLC selection scales with axis count: CompactLogix up to 16 axes, ControlLogix beyond that.

name: TN-02172026-Job1125-MotorCommutation-IG.docx
takeaways: Older projects built in Studio 5000 V33 sometimes have manually-entered Commutation Alignment/Offset values because Rockwell had no motor profile for that motor at the time.
Copying those legacy manual commutation values into a V37 project (which already includes the motor's profile/library) breaks commutation and throws Kinetix 5500 FLT S04 'commutation not configured'.
Symptom progression: servo won't jog at all first, then after touching commutation params to 'match' other axes, it throws FLT S04.

Fix: delete the drive from both the IO tree and the motion axis, re-add the same module under the original name, let it use the auto-detected motor profile's commutation settings (don't manually re-enter the old values), then redownload.

When migrating/replicating a servo config across machines or Studio 5000 versions, don't blindly copy commutation parameters between projects on different Studio 5000/motor-profile versions — verify whether the motor has a native profile first.
